source.title: MM1: Methods, Analysis & Insights from Multimodal LLM Pre-training

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents reading the relevant results.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports downstream benchmark scores for multimodal models at several parameter sizes, extending scale-related downstream evaluation to image-text models. It does not test the original held-out language-model loss laws.
record.gate_note: The paper cites established LLM scaling characteristics when fitting an optimal learning-rate trend from small runs, then uses it to choose settings for larger models. That fit concerns learning rate and downstream 8-shot performance, not held-out cross-entropy scaling. Rows record the separately reported Table 6 downstream scores for MM1 at 3B, 7B, and 30B for 0- and 8-shot evaluation; the 4- and 16-shot scores are left out. No values are reported for held-out cross-entropy loss or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
record.test_reason: Weak test of V6 only. MM1-3B/7B/30B share pre-training data, steps and token order, so Table 6 shows how downstream captioning/VQA scores change with LLM size. There are only three sizes, no fitted law and no prediction. Base LLMs, learning rates and the 30B z-loss also differ. The study does not measure held-out loss scaling or compute allocation.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that their ablation-derived recipe, scaled to 3B/7B/30B dense and MoE LLMs, gives a model family that is SOTA on few-shot pre-training metrics and competitive after SFT. They make no scaling-law claim, and they note zero-shot metrics mainly reflect how well the data mixture matches the task format.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains multimodal image-text models and reports downstream captioning/VQA scores across model sizes; it does not use the original held-out language-loss fitting procedure or test a compute-optimal split.
record.method_sensitivity: Shot count changes the observed size trend: the reported 8-shot scores generally rise with scale, while 0-shot results are mixed. The paper also states that the learning-rate fit uses downstream 8-shot average performance because validation loss was not strongly correlated with downstream task performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Optimal peak learning rate follows a log-linear fit in non-embedding LLM parameters (9M-1.2B), extrapolated to 30B (Eq. 1, Fig. 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimal hyperparameters (learning rate, weight decay) scale as a power law in model size and can be extrapolated.

record.problems: No held-out cross-entropy scaling results, compute-optimal allocation experiment, or quantitative prediction test. The reported downstream scores have no uncertainty estimates, and the size comparisons do not provide a fitted scale-performance law. The study notes that validation loss was not strongly correlated with downstream task performance.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix Table 6 also reports 4-shot and 16-shot scores for the same seven benchmarks and three MM1 sizes; those 42 entries were omitted to stay within 60 rows. SFT benchmark comparisons and SFT ablations are not cross-size tests of downstream scaling.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss measured as a function of parameters, tokens or compute.
No loss extrapolation. The only extrapolation is of optimal learning rate fitted on 8-shot performance, a tool, not a loss prediction.
No fixed-compute sweep or parameter/token allocation.
No LLM depth/width-at-fixed-size comparison. Connector-type ablations concern a different component.
No power-law fit of loss for multimodal training.
Predictability (a fitted relation over orders of magnitude) and the link to pretraining loss are not quantified. There are only three sizes within one order of magnitude.
No comparison of fitting choices or published laws.

missing.what: Statement that validation loss was not strongly correlated with downstream task performance in preliminary experiments, bearing on whether downstream is predictable from loss.
SFT average performance improves consistently with more pre-training steps/data, from checkpoints of the same run.
Doubling image encoder size (ViT-L to ViT-H) gives a modest gain, usually under 1%.

record.verdict_notes: This is a model-building paper. The scale comparisons are confounded by different base LLMs, per-size learning rates and z-loss at 30B, and have no uncertainty estimates. The 4- and 16-shot scores are declared in rows_left_out; 16-shot rises 7B to 30B on all benchmarks. The reader's 'supports' label for all 8-shot rows was too broad, because the 3B to 7B step is mixed.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining cross-entropy loss power laws in parameter count, token count, or compute are measured.
No loss curves fitted on smaller runs are used to predict larger-run losses.
No fixed-compute sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation is tested.
The paper compares visual-language connector and image-processing choices, not the effect of language-model depth and width at fixed parameter count on held-out language loss.
The paper trains multimodal image-text models but does not test whether held-out loss follows the same power-law form across modalities or training regimes.

The study reports downstream multimodal task scores at 3B, 7B, and 30B, but does not fit or validate a predictive relationship with scale or pretraining loss; its scores do not establish predictability across orders of magnitude.
The study does not compare alternative loss-law fitting methods or parameter-counting choices, or test whether loss curves bend from power laws.

relation.reason: The study reports its own downstream results across sizes and explicitly reports weak validation-loss correlation with downstream performance.

tranche.reason: Multimodal captioning and VQA evaluations across model sizes provide results bearing on V6 in a new setting.

source_check.notes: These results establish size trends, not a validated quantitative downstream scaling law. Learning rates and base LLMs differ across sizes, and 30B additionally uses a z-loss; the authors caution that zero-shot scores mainly reflect task-format matching.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: 8-shot pretraining evaluations across MM1-3B, MM1-7B, and MM1-30B
reader_labels.reason: Most scores rise with model size, and all seven listed measures rise from 7B to 30B; see rows r22-r28 and r36-r42. These are benchmark comparisons, not a fitted predictive law.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Scores do not increase consistently with size: several 30B scores fall from 7B, and some 7B scores fall or stay level versus 3B; see rows r15-r21 and r29-r35.
